The receipt photo, proxied from Telegram.

Proxied rather than linked because a Telegram file URL carries the bot
token; handing that to a browser would publish the token to anyone who can
read a network log.

Not written to `audit_log`: the review queue loads these images constantly
and an entry per render would bury the entries that matter. The read is
logged instead, and only a reviewer can ask for one.

The schema, for generating the frontend's types.

Served here rather than at FastAPI's usual public path: the shape of every
admin endpoint is a map for anyone probing the server, and there is no
reason to hand it out unauthenticated.

    openapi-typescript https://<host>/admin/api/v1/system/openapi.json \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" -o src/api/schema.d.ts

schema.title: Response Openapi Schema Admin Api V1 System Openapi Json Get

get.description:
Fast checks only.

Nothing here calls a payment provider or FazerCards: a dashboard that polls
would then spend the shop's rate limit on being looked at. Those get their
own endpoint, and what is reported here is whether they are configured.
Balance and plan, straight from upstream.
Depth of arq's sorted set, split into work that is due and work that waits.

Jobs that ended in an exception.

arq keeps a result for an hour, so this is a recent-failures view rather than
a permanent record; anything older lives only in the logs.

schema.title: Response Failed Jobs Admin Api V1 System Failed Jobs Get

post.description:
Re-enqueue the same call.

arq deletes the job definition once it has failed for good, so the stored
result is the only place the arguments survive - and re-running is a new job,
not a resurrection of the old one.

schema.title: Response Retry Failed Job Admin Api V1 System Failed Jobs  Job Id  Retry Post

post.description:
Send a signed event to our own public URL.

Posting to the public address rather than calling the handler in-process is
the point: this is what proves the tunnel, the TLS certificate and the secret
all still line up.
